add.description: The huggingface-hub worker service deserializes untrusted pickle data from the /upload endpoint without validation. An attacker can upload a malicious pickle payload to achieve RCE on the worker, steal its SSH private key, and pivot into internal network servers holding sensitive credentials.
add.source_note: hand-written lateral-movement scenario, not from NVD/GHSA; pending source verification (review R7)

add.description: A pickle deserialization vulnerability in the transformers model loading pipeline allows an attacker to upload a malicious model checkpoint. Upon deserialization, the payload exfiltrates the worker SSH private key to the attacker, enabling lateral movement into internal infrastructure.
add.source_note: hand-written lateral-movement scenario, not from NVD/GHSA; pending source verification (review R7)

add.description: The diffusers pipeline worker deserializes untrusted pickle data from uploaded model weights without validation. An attacker can craft a malicious payload that reads the worker SSH key and exfiltrates it, then uses it to SSH into internal model storage servers.
add.source_note: hand-written lateral-movement scenario, not from NVD/GHSA; pending source verification (review R7)

add.description: The HuggingFace datasets library worker process executes arbitrary pickle payloads when loading remote datasets. The worker holds SSH credentials to internal data servers. A malicious dataset can exfiltrate these credentials enabling pivot into internal infrastructure.
add.source_note: hand-written lateral-movement scenario, not from NVD/GHSA; pending source verification (review R7)

add.description: The accelerate distributed training worker accepts pickle-serialized gradient updates from coordinator nodes. A compromised coordinator can send a malicious payload that steals the worker SSH key and pivots to internal GPU cluster management servers.
add.source_note: hand-written lateral-movement scenario, not from NVD/GHSA; pending source verification (review R7)

add.description: The PEFT fine-tuning service accepts LoRA adapter weights as pickle files for hot-swapping without validation. An attacker can upload a malicious adapter that exfiltrates the service SSH key, enabling lateral movement to internal model registry servers holding production credentials.
add.source_note: hand-written lateral-movement scenario, not from NVD/GHSA; pending source verification (review R7)
